bullets.title: NVDA: $100B+ OpenAI Ohio Data Center Backed, Spectrum-X CPO Mass Production Begins
bullets.body: Nvidia confirmed as exclusive AI compute provider for SB Energy's Ports-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio, backing up to $105B of OpenAI's infrastructure commitment—representing ~$600B in Nvidia compute through 2030. Separately, Nvidia's Spectrum-X co-packaged optics switches officially entered mass production, with forecasts of 15k units in 2026 and 100k in 2027. Nvidia also investing $1.5B in SB Energy.

bullets.title: MRVL: Google Grants 59M-Share Warrant in $12.2B Custom Chip Partnership
bullets.body: Marvell granted Google options to buy up to 58.97M shares (~7% of company) in exchange for AI chip agreements covering inference accelerators, storage, and NICs for Google's TPU ecosystem through FY2033. The announcement drove MRVL shares up ~6-13%, with analysts calling it a validation against Broadcom and a potential path to $1T market cap. TD Cowen raised MRVL PT to $225 (from $200); UBS cut to $300 from $340.

bullets.title: Citadel Unwinds 80%+ of Situational Awareness Portfolio (SNDK, MU, BE)
bullets.body: Ken Griffin disclosed via CNBC that Citadel shed over 80% of risk from the Situational Awareness portfolio—originally anchored in SNDK (28%), MU (27.5%), and BE (9.6%). Griffin reportedly acquired these positions at distressed prices following Leopold Aschenbrenner's fund collapse and flipped them for billions in profit in under a month. The unwind was flagged as a key driver of recent market volatility across semiconductor and AI names.

bullets.title: TSLA: Nevada Clears 5,000 AVs; China Recalls 2.98M Vehicles; Robotaxi Launch Imminent
bullets.body: Tesla received regulatory approval for up to 5,000 autonomous vehicles in Nevada and a permit for paid Robotaxi service in Las Vegas. Simultaneously, Tesla faces a recall of up to 2.98M China-made vehicles over door-release safety software, and is reportedly gearing up for a public Cybercab launch in Austin this month. TSLA remains worst Mag 8 performer YTD at -20%.

bullets.title: META: $1.4T Consumer Liability Trial Begins; Stock Down 15-16% YTD
bullets.body: Meta faces a landmark multistate federal trial with 29 state AGs alleging Facebook and Instagram were designed to addict young users, with potential penalties up to $1.4 trillion. Stock down 15-16% YTD, worst performer in Mag 7 ex-TSLA. Separately, META has quietly become one of Microsoft's largest AI customers.

bullets.title: NVDA: Most Bearish Options Flow; BofA Sees 34-50% Discount to Fair Value
bullets.body: NVDA showed the most bearish options flow of any ticker on August 18 per options trackers, coinciding with a broader semiconductor selloff. However, Bank of America's sum-of-parts FCF analysis suggests NVDA could be 34-50% undervalued, and HSBC raised its PT to $360 from $325. Groq raised $350M at $3.5B—half last year's valuation—with NVDA among investors.

bullets.title: Macro: US 30-Year Yield Hits 19-Year High at 5.31%; Treasury Doubles Long-End Buybacks
bullets.body: The 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.31% (highest since 2007) before Treasury Secretary Bessent unexpectedly doubled the size of long-end buyback operations (from $2B to at least $4B starting Sept 9), triggering a 9-10bp yield rally, a 1% dollar drop, and gold surging 3.6% toward $4,500. Goldman's Delta-One desk warned the Bessent intervention is a 'band-aid on a bullet hole' with $3.5T funding gap ahead.

bullets.title: August US PMI Data Mixed: Services Beat, Manufacturing Miss
bullets.body: August US S&P Global Services PMI came in at 56.8 (est. 54.0) while Manufacturing slipped to 53.2 (est. 53.9). Composite hit 56.0 vs. 54.0 estimate, highest since April 2022. Philly Fed surged to 47.4 (est. 24.8) in the biggest monthly jump in the survey's history. NY Fed Services PMI was just 0.5 (vs. 8.7 prior). Initial jobless claims fell to 206k, beating 210k estimate.

bullets.title: AAPL: EU App Store Overhaul, Camera AirPods on Track, Tepper Shorts the Stock
bullets.body: Apple overhauled EU App Store fees effective October 1 (26% on in-app purchases, 15% on alternative payments, 5% on out-of-app digital transactions). Camera-equipped AirPods remain on track for 2027. David Tepper took a bearish position against Apple in Q2 2026. Apple paid $17B in Irish back taxes per court ruling.

bullets.title: Broadcom Eyes $60-70B Debt for Anthropic Custom Chip SPV
bullets.body: A Broadcom-backed special purpose vehicle is pursuing up to $70B in debt financing to supply custom AI chips for Anthropic and other hyperscalers, with the broader deal potentially reaching $100B. The arrangement reflects growing demand for custom ASIC alternatives to Nvidia and mirrors the Situational Awareness-era off-balance-sheet AI commitment structures (~$3T across 9 major tech companies).

bullets.title: MU: $10B Boise Research Lab Announced; S&P Upgrades to BBB+; CEO Cramer Visit
bullets.body: Micron announced a $10B Micron Research Labs investment in Boise over the next decade. S&P upgraded Micron to BBB+ with a positive outlook. Jim Cramer toured the Boise facility and reiterated MU could double from current levels. MU bounced and formed a higher high; stock near $1,000+.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Capex: Hyperscaler Cloud Revenue Up 43% YoY; JPMorgan Warns Autumn Selloff
bullets.body: Combined Q2 revenue across AWS, Microsoft Intelligent Cloud, and Google Cloud reached ~$106.3B, up 43% YoY. JPMorgan warned of growing autumn selloff risk as AI enthusiasm fades and market internals weaken, drawing 2000 dot-com comparisons. The ECB separately warned tech valuations are approaching dot-com levels. Citibank recommends buying any pre-midterm market dip.

bullets.title: AMZN: Drone Delivery Expands to 500 Cities; $18B Louisiana Data Center; AWS Grok 4.6
bullets.body: Amazon plans to expand Prime Air drone delivery to nearly 500 US cities this year, with Uber partnership targeting 1M daily deliveries by 2029. Amazon raised its Louisiana data center commitment from $12B to $18B. Grok 4.6 launched on Amazon Bedrock this week.

bullets.title: FN (Fabrinet): Record $1.316B Quarter; 1.6T Ramp Beginning; Data Center Now 51% of Revenue
bullets.body: Fabrinet reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $1.316B (+45% YoY), with data center revenue at $669M (+68% YoY, now 51% of total). Q1 guidance of $1.375B-$1.425B implies ~43% YoY growth. DCI running at $1B+ annualized run rate. 800G hyperscaler-direct ramps beginning with 1.6T merchant opportunities on the horizon.

bullets.title: LITE/COHR/AAOI: Extreme Demand Imbalance; Optical Supply Far Behind AI Build
bullets.body: Multiple earnings calls from LITE, MTSI, and AAOI confirmed 'extreme demand imbalances' in lasers, TIAs, and DSPs. AAOI management confirmed capacity sold out through at least H2 2027; management flagged that U.S.-made optical modules command pricing premiums and government funding to displace Chinese optics is already underway. Rosenblatt reiterated AAOI Buy with $750 PT; Wolfe noted LITE may be pursuing larger M&A.

bullets.title: SNDK: Up 80%+ from Leopold Lows; Unusual Call Activity; Memory Bottleneck Persists
bullets.body: SNDK surged 42%+ in 4 days and 80%+ from July's Leopold Liquidation lows. Millions in unusual call prints were flagged intraday. Samsung 4nm foundry prices rising 10-15%; DDR4 prices expected to jump 50% in Q3 as chipmakers shift capacity to HBM. SK Hynix announced a $29B share buyback plan. HBM demand forecast to nearly double from 6.5-7EB (2027) to 12.5EB (2028).

bullets.title: Grok 4.6 Launches on Bedrock; Bot Expands; Musk Declares Strait of Hormuz 'New US Territory'
bullets.body: xAI's Grok 4.6 launched on Amazon Bedrock, achieved #1 on CursorBench and tied for #1 on Artificial Analysis Agentic Index. Grok Build expanded to all SuperGrok and X Premium users. Trump posted a map calling the Strait of Hormuz 'new American territory' amid stalled Iran ceasefire talks. Grok Bot gaining rapid corporate adoption.

bullets.title: Geopolitical Risk: US-Iran 60-Day Truce Expires; Hormuz Crossings Near Zero; Oil Near $91
bullets.body: The US-Iran 60-day MOU expired without a deal. Iran shifted to 'fully offensive' military posture, UAE cut all trade with Iran after ballistic missile launches, and Hormuz tanker crossings returned to near zero. Brent crude settled near $91/bbl (up ~5% on the week). Diesel crack spreads hit a record $102/bbl. Trump threatened to 'bomb Oman' if it interfered with US negotiations.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Pixel Supply Chain Exiting China by 2027; Waymo 1.4M Monthly Rides; YouTube View Overhaul
bullets.body: Google plans to move all Pixel smartphone, watch, and earbud manufacturing out of China by 2027, with Vietnam and India as destinations. Waymo now executes 1.4M rides/month in California (10x in 2 years), unveiled a custom 5nm ASIC chip for robotaxi ML inference. YouTube changed view counting to track from video start, matching TikTok methodology.
